study_badge: PRISMA 2020 SYSTEMATIC REVIEW · SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DATA
title: Machine-Learning Sepsis Early Warning Systems in Adult Intensive Care Units: A PRISMA 2020 Systematic Review
authors_line: Priya Nair, MD¹; Lukas Meyer, PhD²; Mei-Ling Zhou, MSc¹
affiliations_line: ¹Institute of Critical Care Informatics; ²Dept. of Health Data Science, Synthetic University Hospital

items.title: 01  Clinical Question & PICOS
bullets: Population: Adult medical/surgical ICU admissions (Sepsis-3 criteria).
Intervention: Real-time prospective ML sepsis early warning systems.
Comparator: Standard clinical surveillance or MEWS/SOFA rules.
Outcomes: Diagnostic discrimination (AUROC), time-to-antimicrobials, and 28-day ICU mortality.

items.title: 02  Search & Appraisal Methods
bullets: Databases: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, IEEE Xplore (Jan 2018 – Jun 2026).
Dual independent screening (κ = 0.86); bias appraised via RoB 2 (RCTs) and ROBINS-I (non-randomized studies); certainty graded with GRADE [1].

items.title: 03  PRISMA 2020 Study Selection
items.caption: Figure 1. PRISMA 2020 flow diagram verifying arithmetic count closure across 3,420 records to 18 prospective ICU studies.

items.title: 06  GRADE Certainty & Limitations
bullets: Moderate GRADE certainty for faster antibiotic administration; low-to-moderate certainty for mortality due to workflow co-interventions.
Unstandardized positive-predictive-value reporting limited quantitative pooling across alert thresholds.

items.title: Synthesis Across 18 Prospective Studies (N = 94,300)
paragraphs: Across 6 RCTs and 12 prospective interventional cohorts, multimodal EHR + waveform models achieved median AUROC 0.87 (IQR 0.84–0.90) and shortened antimicrobial initiation by 1.8 hours overall (−2.1 h in huddles-integrated ICUs).

items.title: 04  Prospective Model Discrimination by Architecture
items.caption: Figure 2. Summary prospective ROC profiles across model architecture tiers (18 ICU studies, N = 94,300).

items.title: 05  Evidence Summary by Implementation Tier
items.footnote: RoB 2 applied to randomized trials; ROBINS-I applied to prospective interventional cohorts.

items.title: 07  Conclusions & Implementation Guidance
paragraphs: Prospective ML sepsis alerts reliably accelerate antibiotic administration only when paired with structured nurse-physician escalation workflows and precision-calibrated alert thresholds (PPV ≥0.30) to prevent alarm fatigue [2].

references: [1] Page MJ et al. PRISMA 2020 statement. BMJ 2021;372:n71.
[2] Adams R et al. Nat Med 2022;28:1455–1460.
